options.metric: Sum of number_of_motorist_killed per calendar year.
options.denominator: None; annual fatality count, not a rate.
options.reason: Annual motorist death totals are the most direct crash-data measure of the fatality burden, while making no unsupported exposure claim.
options.answer: Reported motorist deaths fell from 110 in 2013 to 81 in 2025, but these counts cannot establish that per-mile risk declined.
options.interpretation: This framing shows the sum of number_of_motorist_killed across police-reported NYC crashes in each calendar year from 2013 through 2025; the total fell from 110 in 2013 to 81 in 2025, with year-to-year variation. It is a defensible measure of annual motorist fatality burden, but it has no denominator and is not a per-mile rate. The question of whether risk per mile driven declined remains unanswered because the crash file has no miles-driven exposure. Data checks found no missing motorist-killed fields (0/203,742 crashes in 2013 and 0/85,546 in 2025, and zero in every intervening year), and each year had dates spanning January 1 through December 31 including 2025; therefore no in-range crashes were excluded and all were retained in the crash-year totals.

options.metric: 100 times the number of crashes with number_of_motorist_killed greater than zero, divided by all eligible crashes in the calendar year.
options.denominator: All police-reported NYC motor-vehicle crashes with crash_date in that calendar year; each crash counted once.
options.reason: The percentage of crashes involving a motorist death compares fatal-crash frequency with the annual volume of reported crashes.
options.answer: The share of crashes involving a motorist death rose from 0.0501% in 2013 to 0.0877% in 2025, but this is not a per-mile risk measure.
options.interpretation: For each calendar year from 2013 through 2025, this plots 100 times crashes with at least one recorded motorist death divided by all police-reported NYC motor-vehicle crashes, counting each crash once; the share rose from 102/203,742 (0.0501%) in 2013 to 75/85,546 (0.0877%) in 2025. This is a defensible within-reported-crash frequency measure, but it does not establish whether deaths per mile or an individual motorist's risk changed because miles driven and the population of motorists are not in the file. Data checks found no missing or impossible negative motorist-killed fields (0/203,742 crashes in 2013 and 0/85,546 in 2025, and zero in every intervening year), and each year had dates spanning January 1 through December 31 including 2025. Consequently all in-range crashes were included in the denominators, with none excluded or assigned to an unknown category.
